Status Detail.value: September 2026: MidAmerican told Adair County supervisors that construction began in April 2026. The Iowa Department of Natural Resources issued air construction permits for units 1 and 2 on April 30, 2026, and for a third turbine on June 11, 2026.
Status Detail.note: The Western Iowa Today report and the state air permit page for Orient Energy Center give these facts.

Capacity (MW).note: A MidAmerican news release says the Orient Energy Center would add 465 MW, from two turbines. That is 232.5 MW each, which matches GEM.

Start year.note: MidAmerican's release says the plant would generate power beginning in 2028. This matches GEM.

City.note: A KMAland article says the plant would be built south of the town of Orient in Adair County. The site is rural, so City is the nearest town.

qa.recommendation: Add unit 3. The state issued air permit 26-A-246 on June 11, 2026 for a third turbine, under a project called Add Unit 3. MidAmerican's fact sheet says the plant has three turbines and up to 700 MW, with unit 3 in service in spring 2029.
qa.note: The two-unit figure of 465 MW in the 2025 news release came before the third turbine was permitted.

qa.recommendation: The IRP study lists 233 MW peaking plants in 2028 and 2029. The first two turbines here already add up to about 465 MW. No separate placeholder looks needed for them.
qa.note: The study table shows 233 MW in each of 2028 and 2029. These match the two Orient turbines.

qa.recommendation: Check whether the new unit 3 is the same plant as MidAmerican 2024 IRP power station 1 (L100001064541), a 232.5 MW placeholder for 2031. If so, retire the placeholder instead of keeping both.
qa.note: The plan placeholder has the same size as each Orient turbine.

qa.recommendation: Consider adding fuel oil as a second fuel. The state air permits allow start-ups and shutdowns on fuel oil.
qa.note: The permits name no turbine maker or model, so Equipment stays blank.

newunits.note: The state issued air permit 26-A-246 on June 11, 2026 for a third combustion turbine at Orient, with the same heat input as units 1 and 2. MidAmerican's fact sheet says the plant will have up to 700 MW with unit 3 in service in spring 2029. The capacity of 232.5 MW is worked out, not stated: the turbines are the same size, and 700 MW less the 465 MW of units 1 and 2 leaves about 235 MW. The status is pre-construction because the permit is issued but the turbine is not yet installed. The owner is MidAmerican Energy, the same as the other units; please copy it from them.
